concepts.title: NumPy: Array, Vectorization และ Broadcasting
concepts.covers: Why ndarray beats a Python list (one dtype, contiguous memory, vectorized math); creating arrays (np.array, arange, linspace, zeros, ones); shape, ndim, dtype, size; element-wise math without loops; indexing, slicing, boolean masks (a[a > 80]) and np.where; 2-D arrays, m[0, :], m[:, 1], aggregation with axis=0 (down columns) vs axis=1 (across rows); broadcasting a row vector against a matrix (subtract column means); reshape; reproducible randomness with rng = np.random.default_rng(42) (integers, normal, choice). Example file ~/projects/ds-lab/numpy_scores.py: rng = default_rng(42), scores = rng.integers(40, 101, size=(6, 3)) for 6 students x 3 subjects (คณิต, วิทย์, อังกฤษ), prints the matrix, shape, per-subject mean (axis=0), per-student mean (axis=1, rounded 1 dp), count of scores >= 80 via boolean mask, centred scores (scores - scores.mean(axis=0)) rounded, and np.where(scores >= 50, 'ผ่าน', 'ไม่ผ่าน'). Mistakes: ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (6,3) (6,); IndexError: index 3 is out of bounds for axis 1 with size 3; confusing axis=0/axis=1; integer division/dtype surprises (np.array([1,2]) / 2 is float64).

concepts.title: pandas พื้นฐาน: Series, DataFrame, read_csv และการเลือกข้อมูล
concepts.covers: Series vs DataFrame and the Index; pd.read_csv with parse_dates and encoding; first look: head, shape, info, dtypes, describe, value_counts; selecting columns df['qty'] and df[['menu','qty']]; loc (labels) vs iloc (positions); boolean filtering with &, |, ~ and parentheses, isin, between, query; new columns with vectorized math (amount = qty * unit_price) and assign; sort_values, nlargest, rename; pandas 3 behaviour: text columns have dtype str, Copy-on-Write means chained assignment df[mask]['qty'] = 0 does nothing (ChainedAssignmentError warning), so use df.loc[mask, 'qty'] = 0. Uses data/sales.csv exactly as in notes. Example file ~/projects/ds-lab/pandas_basics.py: loads sales.csv, prints shape, dtypes, head(3), adds amount, filters QR payments with qty >= 2 sorted by amount desc, the same filter written with query(), the 3 largest orders with nlargest, and df.loc[df['order_id'] == 4, ['menu','amount']]. Mistakes: KeyError: 'Qty' (wrong column name/case); ValueError: The truth value of a Series is ambiguous (using and/or instead of &/|); TypeError from comparing a str column with a number; ChainedAssignmentError warning and the unchanged DataFrame.

concepts.title: ทำความสะอาดข้อมูล: Missing Data, ข้อมูลซ้ำ, ชนิดข้อมูล และวันเวลา
concepts.covers: Detecting problems with isna().sum(), duplicated(), dtypes and unique(); dropna vs fillna (median, mode, constant) and when each is justified; drop_duplicates; str.strip, str.replace and pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce'); astype; pd.to_datetime with format, .dt.day_name(), .dt.month, and resample('D') / groupby by date; documenting each cleaning decision. Example data file ~/projects/ds-lab/data/sales_raw.csv = the 12 rows of sales.csv plus exactly these problems: order 3 has an empty qty; order 5 appears twice (13 data rows in total); order 7 menu is written with surrounding spaces ' อเมริกาโน่ร้อน '; order 10 unit_price is the text '65 บาท'. Example file ~/projects/ds-lab/clean_sales.py prints the problems found (missing count, duplicate count, dtypes), cleans them (drop duplicate, strip menu, strip ' บาท' and convert to number, fill missing qty with the median of qty and explain), then asserts the cleaned frame has 12 rows and no missing values, prints daily revenue with resample('D') and revenue by day name. Mistakes: ValueError: could not convert string to float: '65 บาท'; dates parsed as str (dtype str) so .dt fails with AttributeError: Can only use .dt accessor with datetimelike values; fillna on a copy with no effect; silently dropping too many rows with dropna().

concepts.title: groupby, merge, pivot_table และการอ่านข้อมูลจาก SQLite
concepts.covers: Split-apply-combine with groupby and named aggregation agg(orders=('order_id','count'), ...); merge with on/how (inner, left, outer) and validate='many_to_one', checking row counts before/after; pivot_table with index, columns, values, aggfunc='sum', fill_value=0, margins=True; pd.crosstab; melt back to long form; SQLite: build data/shop.db with to_sql (tables sales and branches), then pd.read_sql with sqlite3.connect and a parameterized query (params=(...)) instead of f-strings to avoid SQL injection; when to aggregate in SQL vs pandas. Example file ~/projects/ds-lab/shop_db.py: writes both CSVs into data/shop.db, runs SQL 'SELECT b.branch_name, SUM(s.qty * s.unit_price) AS revenue FROM sales s JOIN branches b USING (branch_id) WHERE s.date >= ? GROUP BY b.branch_name ORDER BY revenue DESC' with params=('2026-10-01',), prints it, then reproduces the same numbers with merge + groupby and asserts they match, then prints pivot_table revenue by branch_name x category with fill_value=0 and margins. Expected totals must agree with Part 1: สยาม 680, นิมมาน 385, อารีย์ 245, total 1310. Mistakes: MergeError from validate when keys are duplicated; row explosion after a many-to-many merge; KeyError on a column that became the index after groupby (use reset_index or as_index=False); sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: sales (wrong working directory / path).

concepts.title: EDA และการทำกราฟด้วย matplotlib
concepts.covers: Goals of EDA; fig, ax = plt.subplots(); titles, axis labels with units; choosing the chart: histogram, box plot, bar, line, scatter; df.corr(numeric_only=True) and correlation is not causation; saving with fig.savefig('charts/<name>.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight') and plt.close(fig); in WSL without python3-tk the backend is agg (print matplotlib.get_backend()); Thai text in charts needs fonts-thai-tlwg and rcParams['font.family'] = 'Loma', otherwise UserWarning: Glyph ... missing from font(s) DejaVu Sans; keep axis labels in English to avoid the font issue in code examples. Example file ~/projects/ds-lab/eda_diabetes.py: load_diabetes(as_frame=True) (scaled features, target = disease progression after one year), prints describe() of target, bmi and bp, the top 3 correlations with target, and saves 4 charts (target histogram, bmi vs target scatter, box plot of target split by bmi above/below median, bar chart of correlations) into charts/. Because images cannot be embedded, describe each chart in Thai and show the numbers that back it. Mistakes: FileNotFoundError when charts/ does not exist (use Path('charts').mkdir(exist_ok=True)); empty PNG because savefig was called after plt.show(); Thai glyph warning; overlapping labels fixed with fig.tight_layout().

concepts.title: สถิติเชิงพรรณนา ความน่าจะเป็น และ Central Limit Theorem
concepts.covers: Mean vs median vs mode and skewed data; variance, standard deviation, quartiles, IQR and the 1.5 x IQR outlier rule; basic probability, conditional probability and Bayes' theorem with a medical-test example (prevalence 1%, sensitivity 95%, false positive rate 5% -> P(sick | positive) about 16%); distributions with scipy.stats (norm, binom, poisson) .pmf/.cdf/.ppf/.rvs(random_state=42); sampling and sampling bias; CLT by simulation: draw 10,000 samples of size 5, 30 and 100 from a skewed (exponential) population with default_rng(42), show the mean and std of the sample means and that the std shrinks like sigma/sqrt(n) (standard error). Example file ~/projects/ds-lab/stats_clt.py: simulated salaries rng.lognormal(mean=10.2, sigma=0.5, size=1000) printed as mean/median/IQR and outlier count, the Bayes calculation, P(X <= 2) for Poisson(3) customers per 10 minutes, and the CLT table, saving charts/clt.png. Mistakes: using np.std (ddof=0) vs pandas .std() (ddof=1) and getting different numbers; reporting the mean of skewed money data; misreading conditional probability P(A|B) as P(B|A).

concepts.title: Confidence Interval, Hypothesis Test และ A/B Test ด้วย scipy.stats
concepts.covers: Correct meaning of a 95% CI and of a p-value; H0/H1 and alpha chosen before looking; stats.t.interval for a mean and stats.bootstrap for any statistic (random_state=42); choosing a test: ttest_ind (Welch, equal_var=False), ttest_rel, chi2_contingency, mannwhitneyu; Type I/II errors and power; A/B test design (randomization, primary metric, sample size fixed in advance, no peeking); statistical vs practical significance and effect size. Example file ~/projects/ds-lab/ab_report.py extends Part 1's ab_test.py with the SAME numbers (A: 82 of 1000, B: 113 of 1000; chi2 = 5.114, p = 0.0237 with Yates correction) and adds: the difference in conversion (3.1 percentage points) with a 95% CI using the normal approximation, a bootstrap CI of the difference, and a Welch t-test that 'mean radius' differs between malignant and benign tumours in load_breast_cancer, ending with a 3-sentence plain-Thai conclusion. Mistakes: interpreting p = 0.02 as '2% chance H0 is true'; stopping the test early when p < 0.05; using ttest_ind on paired data; passing percentages instead of counts to chi2_contingency.

concepts.title: Workflow ของ scikit-learn และ Regression: Pipeline, ColumnTransformer, Cross-validation, MAE/RMSE/R²
concepts.covers: The estimator API (fit, predict, score, fit_transform/transform); train_test_split(test_size=0.2, random_state=42); DummyRegressor baseline; StandardScaler, OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore'), SimpleImputer; ColumnTransformer + Pipeline to prevent data leakage; cross_val_score / cross_validate with KFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=42) and scoring='neg_root_mean_squared_error'; LinearRegression coef_/intercept_, Ridge and Lasso with alpha; metrics mean_absolute_error, root_mean_squared_error (scikit-learn 1.9 removed squared=False: TypeError ... unexpected keyword argument 'squared'), r2_score; residuals; joblib.dump/load and the warning never to load untrusted pickle files. Example file ~/projects/ds-lab/regression_diabetes.py: load_diabetes(as_frame=True), compares DummyRegressor, LinearRegression, Ridge(alpha=1.0) and Lasso(alpha=0.1) in pipelines with 5-fold CV RMSE (mean ± std), then the best on the test set with MAE, RMSE, R², the 3 largest coefficients, counts Lasso non-zero coefficients, saves charts/residuals.png and the model to models/ridge.joblib, reloads it and checks identical predictions. A second short file columns_demo.py shows a ColumnTransformer on data/sales.csv (scale qty and unit_price, one-hot branch_id and payment) and prints get_feature_names_out(). Mistakes: ValueError: Expected 2D array, got 1D array instead (pass df[['bmi']] not df['bmi']); scaling before splitting (leakage); negative scores from neg_* scoring misread; ValueError: could not convert string to float when a text column reaches the model without encoding.

concepts.title: Classification และการวัดผล: Confusion Matrix, Precision, Recall, ROC-AUC และข้อมูลไม่สมดุล
concepts.covers: LogisticRegression (sigmoid, predict_proba vs predict at 0.5) and DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=3) with export_text; confusion_matrix layout (rows = actual, columns = predicted), TP/FP/TN/FN; precision, recall, F1 and classification_report; roc_auc_score, average_precision_score and why PR curves suit rare classes; class imbalance with stratify, class_weight='balanced' and threshold tuning from predict_proba; choosing a threshold from business costs; multiclass averages macro vs weighted (load_wine). Example file ~/projects/ds-lab/classify_cancer.py continues Part 1's first_model.py with the SAME split (load_breast_cancer, test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=42; Part 1 printed baseline 0.632 and logistic test accuracy 0.982): note that in this dataset target 0 = malignant, 1 = benign, so to treat malignant as the positive class use y_pos = 1 - y or pos_label=0 and say so clearly; prints confusion matrix, classification_report, ROC-AUC, and a table of precision/recall for thresholds 0.3, 0.5, 0.7. Second file imbalance_demo.py: make_classification(n_samples=2000, weights=[0.95], random_state=42) comparing DummyClassifier, LogisticRegression and LogisticRegression(class_weight='balanced') on accuracy, recall and ROC-AUC. Mistakes: reporting accuracy on imbalanced data; mixing up which label is positive; UndefinedMetricWarning: Precision is ill-defined and being set to 0.0 when a model predicts no positives; ConvergenceWarning: lbfgs failed to converge (scale features or raise max_iter).

concepts.title: Overfitting, Tree Ensemble, GridSearchCV และ Permutation Importance
concepts.covers: Underfitting vs overfitting via the train/test gap; bias-variance trade-off; validation_curve over DecisionTree max_depth 1..15; RandomForestClassifier (bagging; n_estimators, max_depth, min_samples_leaf) and HistGradientBoostingClassifier (boosting; learning_rate, max_iter, early_stopping, native NaN support); GridSearchCV over a Pipeline with step__param names, StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=42), scoring='roc_auc', n_jobs=-1, best_params_, best_score_, then ONE final test-set evaluation; estimating fit count (grid size x folds); model interpretation with feature_importances_ vs sklearn.inspection.permutation_importance(n_repeats=10, random_state=42) on the test set, and why importance is not causation. Example file ~/projects/ds-lab/tune_forest.py on load_breast_cancer (same split as c09): prints train vs CV score for max_depth 1, 3, 6, 10, None; compares LogisticRegression, RandomForest and HistGradientBoosting by 5-fold ROC-AUC with fit time (time varies by machine, say so); GridSearchCV over max_depth [3, 6, None] x min_samples_leaf [1, 5] (6 combinations x 5 folds = 30 fits); prints best params, best CV score, test ROC-AUC, and the top 5 features by impurity importance and by permutation importance side by side. Mistakes: tuning on the test set; ValueError: Invalid parameter 'max_depth' for estimator Pipeline (missing the model__ prefix); very long runtimes from oversized grids; trusting impurity importance for high-cardinality features.

concepts.title: Unsupervised Learning: k-means และ PCA
concepts.covers: What unsupervised learning is for (customer segmentation, exploration); k-means algorithm step by step, the need to scale first, KMeans(n_clusters=k, n_init=10, random_state=42); choosing k with inertia_ (elbow) and silhouette_score; profiling clusters with groupby means and naming them; PCA(n_components=2), explained_variance_ratio_, components_ loadings, scatter of the 2 components coloured by cluster; limits (k-means assumes round clusters; PCA is linear); comparing clusters with the true wine classes using pd.crosstab and adjusted_rand_score as a sanity check only. Example file ~/projects/ds-lab/wine_clusters.py: load_wine(as_frame=True) without the target for fitting, StandardScaler, k = 2..8 table of inertia and silhouette, chooses k = 3 with reasoning from the printed numbers, prints cluster sizes and mean of 4 key features per cluster, PCA explained variance of PC1 and PC2, crosstab vs the real class, saves charts/wine_elbow.png and charts/wine_pca.png. Mistakes: forgetting to scale so one large-valued feature (proline) dominates; different cluster numbering between runs without random_state; ValueError: Number of labels is 1 in silhouette_score with k = 1; treating PCA components as original features.

concepts.title: Neural Network เบื้องต้น: จาก Gradient Descent สู่ MLPClassifier และ PyTorch
concepts.covers: Loss (MSE) and gradient descent written in NumPy for y = 3x + 5 + noise (default_rng(42), learning rate 0.05, printing loss every 100 steps, final m and c near 3 and 5); a neuron = dot product + bias + activation (ReLU); layers and backpropagation intuition; MLPClassifier(hidden_layer_sizes=(64,), max_iter=500, random_state=42) in a Pipeline with StandardScaler on load_digits (1,797 images 8x8, test_size=0.2, stratify, random_state=42) vs LogisticRegression; PyTorch 2.14.1 CPU: tensors, dtype float32, autograd, nn.Sequential(Linear(64,64), ReLU(), Linear(64,10)), nn.CrossEntropyLoss, torch.optim.Adam(lr=1e-3), TensorDataset + DataLoader(batch_size=64, shuffle=True), the 5-line training loop (zero_grad, forward, loss, backward, step), model.train()/model.eval(), torch.no_grad(), torch.manual_seed(42); when to prefer trees over neural nets on tabular data. Example files ~/projects/ds-lab/gd_line.py, ~/projects/ds-lab/mlp_digits.py and ~/projects/ds-lab/torch_digits.py (20 epochs, loss printed every 5 epochs, final test accuracy). Install command: python3 -m pip install "torch==2.14.1" --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu (about 770 MB in the venv; the default PyPI wheel on Linux is the CUDA build and is several GB). PyTorch losses/accuracies may differ slightly across CPUs even with a seed; say so in Thai. Mistakes: RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (...) from an input that was not flattened to 64 features (run it to get the exact shapes); RuntimeError: expected scalar type Float but found Double (use float32); forgetting optimizer.zero_grad() so gradients accumulate; ConvergenceWarning from MLPClassifier with too few iterations; learning rate too high giving loss = nan.

mini_project.name: Churn ML: ทำนายสมาชิกฟิตเนสที่จะยกเลิกสมาชิก (End-to-End ML Project)
mini_project.summary: A complete, reproducible classification project for a fictional Thai fitness chain 'FitSomchai' (5 provinces). Problem framing (predict which members will cancel so the retention team can call them first; primary metric = recall of the churn class at an acceptable precision, ROC-AUC to compare models), deterministic synthetic data generated by generate_members.py (seed 42, 2,000 members, churn rate 13.6%, 60 missing avg_session_min values) saved to CSV and SQLite, loading with pd.read_sql, cleaning, EDA with 4+ charts saved to reports/figures/, feature engineering, baseline vs Logistic Regression vs Random Forest vs HistGradientBoosting with StratifiedKFold(5), GridSearchCV on the best family, one final test-set evaluation (confusion matrix, classification report, ROC-AUC, cost-based threshold), fairness check of recall per province, permutation importance, an optional LLM step that drafts the executive summary from aggregate metrics only (mock mode without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, no personal data sent), and a README written as a report with conclusions and limitations, pushed to GitHub.
mini_project.structure:
churn-ml/
  README.md
  requirements.txt
  .gitignore            (.venv/, data/*.db, data/*.csv, models/, __pycache__/, .env)
  src/
    generate_members.py
    load_data.py
    eda.py
    features.py
    train.py
    evaluate.py
    report_assistant.py
  data/                 (generated, not committed)
  models/               (churn_model.joblib, not committed)
  reports/
    figures/            (PNG charts)
    metrics.json
features: generate_members.py recreates exactly the same data every run (seed 42), writing data/members.csv and table members in data/members.db
load_data.py reads from SQLite with pd.read_sql and a parameterized query; validates schema and row count 2000

eda.py prints churn rate overall and by plan, province, payment_method, has_trainer; saves at least 4 charts (churn by plan bar, visits_last_30d histogram by churn, support_tickets vs churn rate, correlation bar) to reports/figures/

features.py adds fee_per_visit = monthly_fee / (visits_last_30d + 1) and tenure_bucket; ColumnTransformer with SimpleImputer(median) + StandardScaler for numeric and OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore') for province, plan, payment_method

train.py compares DummyClassifier(most_frequent), LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, class_weight='balanced'), RandomForestClassifier(random_state=42, class_weight='balanced') and HistGradientBoostingClassifier(random_state=42) by 5-fold StratifiedKFold ROC-AUC on the training split (train_test_split test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=42); GridSearchCV on the winner; saves models/churn_model.joblib

evaluate.py evaluates once on the test split: confusion matrix, classification_report, ROC-AUC, average precision, threshold table (0.2 to 0.6) with a cost rule (missed churner costs 3 x a wasted call), recall per province, permutation importance top 8; writes reports/metrics.json

report_assistant.py sends only aggregate numbers from reports/metrics.json to Claude (anthropic 1.15.0, model from CLAUDE_MODEL default claude-opus-5-5, follow dev/AI_GUIDE.md) to draft a 5-sentence Thai executive summary; switches to a deterministic mock summary automatically when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is missing

README.md as a report: problem, data (synthetic, why), method, results table vs baseline, chosen threshold and why, fairness check, limitations (synthetic data, no time dimension, correlation is not causation), how to reproduce (5 commands), PDPA note
mini_project.stack: Python 3.12.3, numpy 2.5.4, pandas 3.1.0, matplotlib 3.11.2, scipy 1.18.1, scikit-learn 1.9.1 (joblib 1.6.0), sqlite3 (SQLite 3.45.1), anthropic 1.15.0 (optional, mock mode), Git 2.43.0 + GitHub
mini_project.generator_script:
# สร้างข้อมูลสมาชิกฟิตเนสจำลอง (Synthetic) ด้วย Seed คงที่ รันกี่ครั้งก็ได้ไฟล์เหมือนเดิม
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

SEED = 42
N = 2000
rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)

provinces = np.array(["กรุงเทพมหานคร", "เชียงใหม่", "ขอนแก่น", "ชลบุรี", "ภูเก็ต"])
plans = np.array(["basic", "standard", "premium"])
fees = {"basic": 590, "standard": 990, "premium": 1590}

province = rng.choice(provinces, N, p=[0.45, 0.15, 0.12, 0.16, 0.12])
plan = rng.choice(plans, N, p=[0.5, 0.35, 0.15])
age = rng.integers(18, 66, N)
tenure_months = rng.integers(1, 49, N)
visits_last_30d = rng.poisson(np.select([plan == "basic", plan == "standard"], [6, 9], 12))
avg_session_min = rng.normal(55, 15, N).clip(15, 120).round(1)
classes_booked = rng.poisson(np.where(plan == "premium", 4, 1.5))
support_tickets = rng.poisson(0.6, N)
payment_method = rng.choice(["card", "qr", "cash"], N, p=[0.45, 0.4, 0.15])
has_trainer = (rng.random(N) < np.where(plan == "premium", 0.5, 0.15)).astype(int)
signup_date = pd.Timestamp("2026-10-01") - pd.to_timedelta(tenure_months * 30, unit="D")

# โอกาสยกเลิกสมาชิก: มาน้อย ร้องเรียนบ่อย อายุสมาชิกสั้น จ่ายเงินสด ยิ่งมีโอกาสยกเลิกสูง
logit = (
    0.2
    - 0.22 * visits_last_30d
    + 0.55 * support_tickets
    - 0.035 * tenure_months
    + 0.6 * (payment_method == "cash")
    + 0.35 * (plan == "basic")
    - 0.7 * has_trainer
    - 0.1 * classes_booked
)
churned = (rng.random(N) < 1 / (1 + np.exp(-logit))).astype(int)

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "member_id": [f"M{i:04d}" for i in range(1, N + 1)],
    "signup_date": signup_date.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
    "province": province,
    "plan": plan,
    "monthly_fee": [fees[p] for p in plan],
    "age": age,
    "tenure_months": tenure_months,
    "visits_last_30d": visits_last_30d,
    "avg_session_min": avg_session_min,
    "classes_booked": classes_booked,
    "support_tickets": support_tickets,
    "payment_method": payment_method,
    "has_trainer": has_trainer,
    "churned": churned,
})
# ทำให้ข้อมูลเหมือนของจริง: บางแถวไม่มีค่า avg_session_min (เครื่องสแกนบัตรไม่ได้บันทึก)
df.loc[rng.choice(N, 60, replace=False), "avg_session_min"] = np.nan

out = Path("data")
out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
df.to_csv(out / "members.csv", index=False)
with sqlite3.connect(out / "members.db") as con:
    df.to_sql("members", con, if_exists="replace", index=False)

print("บันทึก", len(df), "แถว ลง data/members.csv และ data/members.db")
print("อัตรายกเลิกสมาชิก (churn rate):", f"{df['churned'].mean():.1%}")
print("ค่าว่างใน avg_session_min:", df["avg_session_min"].isna().sum())

Datasets must work offline: sklearn load_iris, load_wine, load_breast_cancer, load_diabetes, load_digits (as_frame=True when a DataFrame helps), make_classification / make_regression with random_state=42, or the scripts in this outline. Never use fetch_* functions.

Randomness: always np.random.default_rng(42), random_state=42, torch.manual_seed(42). Splits: train_test_split(test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=y for classification). CV: KFold/StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42) unless reproducing Part 1's cv=5.
load_breast_cancer target: 0 = malignant (มะเร็ง/ชนิดร้าย), 1 = benign (ไม่ร้าย). When the lesson treats malignant as the positive class, state it and use pos_label=0 or y_pos = 1 - y consistently.

Charts: create with fig, ax = plt.subplots(), save to charts/<name>.png (Mini Project: reports/figures/) with dpi=150 and bbox_inches='tight', then plt.close(fig). Pages cannot show images: describe each chart in Thai (what is on each axis, the shape you should see) and print the numbers behind it. Use English axis labels in code to avoid the Thai-font warning; explain fonts-thai-tlwg + font.family 'Loma' once (Part 1 Step 5 does).

Run scripts as python3 file.py inside the activated venv. Command blocks contain commands only; show the (.venv) prompt only inside output blocks when needed. Install blocks come first. pandas 3.1 specifics to respect: text columns have dtype str (not object) in info()/dtypes output; Copy-on-Write is the default, chained assignment never works (ChainedAssignmentError warning); use .loc. scikit-learn 1.9 specifics: use root_mean_squared_error (mean_squared_error(squared=False) raises TypeError); KMeans n_init default is 'auto' but write n_init=10 explicitly.
